contested.reason: There is no `as any` cast in the file. The detector's regex /\bas\s+any\b/ (scripts/static-gate.mjs:137) is matched line-wise against added lines with no comment awareness, and the line it matched is prose inside a // comment: 'membership that somehow lacks it is answered the same as any other stranger.' — the English words 'the same as any other', not a type assertion. Checks: (1) `grep -n 'as any' apps/api/src/portal/portal-home.service.ts` returns exactly one hit, line 111, and that line begins with '//'; (2) a TypeScript 'as any' assertion requires an expression to its left, and the token to the left here is the word 'same'; (3) the file contains no @ts-ignore, no @ts-expect-error, no eslint-disable and no 'as unknown as', and `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/api/tsconfig.json` is clean, so nothing in it suppresses a type error. The class of defect is demonstrable from the gate's own output: the same regex also matches lines 2422-2467 of this run's baseRef...HEAD diff, which are the static gate's previously committed verdict JSON quoting its own message — a detector that flags its own prose is matching English, not code. The mechanism fix belongs in scripts/static-gate.mjs (skip lines whose match falls inside a // or /* */ comment), on a build/* branch rather than this run's; rewording the comment would make this gate green while leaving the next occurrence of the words 'as any other' to fail the same way.

notes.claim: REQ-01-018 falls back to Organization.countryCode for a member who states no country, and the README presents that chain as the one time-off already owns. PATCH-012 removed that fallback from the product and the code holds no such chain, so the portal would answer a different country than every other screen for the same member.

witness.detail: specs/portal/README.md §Related Areas: 'specs/time-off/ — owns the country-resolution chain the holidays block uses: a country stated on the membership, falling back to Organization.countryCode. REQ-01-018 states that chain in full rather than pointing at it.' specs/patches/PATCH-012-a-member-states-their-own-country-or-none.md §The rule: 'THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve a member's holiday country from the country stated on their own membership, and from nothing else' and 'THE SYSTEM SHALL pay a member with no resolved country the global holidays only — the rows carrying no country — in the Holidays summary, in the time-off calendar, in the holiday list read as mine, and in Amounts Owed.' The code agrees with the patch: packages/validation/src/reports.ts:566-573 (`resolveMemberHolidayCountry` reads only `membershipCountry` and returns null when it is blank) and apps/api/src/holidays/holidays.service.ts:111-118 ('PATCH-012 — the caller's own stated country. A caller who states none sees the global rows only, rather than the ones the organization's country would have lent them'). Scenario: an organization with countryCode 'US' and a member whose membership states none, with one US holiday and one global holiday seeded. GET .../holidays?scope=mine answers the global holiday alone; GET .../portal/home under REQ-01-018 answers both, and TC-01-INT-07 asserts it must.

notes.suggestedFix: Either drop the third link — REQ-01-018 resolves the membership's country and nothing else, REQ-01-019 becomes 'a member who states no country', TC-01-INT-07's second leg changes — or state deliberately, in this spec's own text, that the portal reinstates the organization fallback that PATCH-012 removed and why one screen may answer a different country than the calendar and the payroll report do. The README's Related Areas sentence is false either way and must go.

notes.claim: The screen replaces the holidays list with PORTAL_MESSAGES.noCountry whenever no country is stated, while REQ-01-019 answers that same caller the global holidays. witness.detail: specs/portal/01-home.contracts.md:286 — 'Q1 answered, no country | The holidays list is replaced by PORTAL_MESSAGES.noCountry and a link to the profile.' specs/portal/01-home.md:175 — 'IF the caller's membership states no country, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL answer only the holidays whose countryCode is null.' Concrete case: an organization with one holiday whose countryCode is null, and a member whose membership states no country. GET .../portal/home answers holidays.countryCode null and holidays.upcoming carrying that one row — the API is built and TC-01-INT-07 asserts exactly this. The screen, built to the states table, draws 'Nobody has stated your country, so no holiday calendar reaches you.' in place of the list and never draws the row. Both statements are implemented as written; they describe different screens for one body.

notes.suggestedFix: Decide which is true and say so in one place: either the sentence is drawn only when holidays.upcoming is empty (and the list is drawn whenever it is not, whatever countryCode says), or REQ-01-019 stops answering global rows to a member with no country. The implementation follows the states table today because that table is determinate; no case in the bundle distinguishes the two readings, because every case with no country also has no global holiday.
